hypothesis: A small fixed set of transparent momentum, contrarian, volatility-gated, breakout, and wick-reversal rules may improve net returns over a no-trade control on a strictly later chronological test segment.
primary_metric: mean net return per test bar after declared 0.2-pip round-trip cost

signal_definitions.MOMENTUM_3: sign of sum of previous 3 closed-bar returns
signal_definitions.CONTRARIAN_3: opposite sign of sum of previous 3 closed-bar returns
signal_definitions.MOMENTUM_12: sign of sum of previous 12 closed-bar returns
signal_definitions.CONTRARIAN_12: opposite sign of sum of previous 12 closed-bar returns
signal_definitions.Z15_MOMENTUM_3: momentum over 3 bars only when absolute 3-bar return divided by trailing 24-bar standard deviation times sqrt(3) is at least 1.5
signal_definitions.Z15_CONTRARIAN_3: contrarian version of the same fixed volatility gate
signal_definitions.BREAKOUT_12: trade only when current closed price breaks the previous 12 bars high or low
signal_definitions.WICK_REVERSAL_1: fixed long-wick rejection rule using only the just-closed candle

verdict_rule: Candidate survives only if it has at least 200 test trades, the 95% block-bootstrap lower bound of mean net return per test bar is above zero at 0.2 pip, and its BH-corrected test is rejected. No-trade is the control, never a survivor.
scientific_boundary: Historical screen only. Any survivor requires a separate frozen live-paper evaluation with fresh data, ledger-backed resolutions, and realistic broker-specific costs before any profitability claim.
